newsitem.title: CAMBODIA: Three dead in Phnom demo blast - police.
newsitem.headline: Three dead in Phnom demo blast - police.

text.p: At least three people were killed and five seriously injured when explosions rocked an opposition demonstration in the Cambodian capital on Sunday, police and witnesses said.
They said two grenades were thrown from a car that sped up to the demonstration outside the Cambodian National Assembly. A bomb also appeared to have exploded in a nearby food vendor's cart.
The demonstration was called by opposition leader Sam Rainsy who was nearby when the explosions went off. He was whisked away by aides and his wife Tioulong Saumura told Reuters he was safe.
Many of the dead and injured had been near the food vendor's cart. Blood and placards littered the ground and heavily armed police sealed off the area.
Rainsy's officially unrecognised Khmer Nation Party called the demonstration to press for the judiciary to be independent of the ruling Cambodian People's Party.
Rainsy was ousted as finance minister in 1994 and formed the KNP in November 1995.
